description: Keep only films whose rental duration is strictly more than 5 days, so films with exactly 5 days are left out.

d.request: Filter to films with `rental_duration` > 5, then group by `rating`. For each rating, return the rating, the average of `rental_rate / rental_duration` across films with nonmissing values, the number of films in the group, and that average divided by the unweighted mean of the nonmissing per-rating averages across all ratings. Return no rows if the benchmark is missing, and do not round values.
d.sql:
WITH rating_averages AS (
  SELECT rating,
         AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_duration,
         COUNT(*) AS film_count
  FROM film
  WHERE rental_duration > 5
    AND rental_rate IS NOT NULL
    AND rental_duration IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY rating
), benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_duration) AS unweighted_mean
  FROM rating_averages
)
SELECT ra.rating,
       ra.avg_rate_per_duration,
       ra.film_count,
       ra.avg_rate_per_duration / b.unweighted_mean AS relative_to_mean
FROM rating_averages ra
CROSS JOIN benchmark b
WHERE b.unweighted_mean IS NOT NULL;

a.request: Looking only at films whose `rental_duration` is more than 5 days, group them by `rating`. For each rating, show the rating, the average per film of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values), the number of films, and that average divided by an overall benchmark. The benchmark is the plain unweighted mean of the per-rating averages across all ratings, ignoring any missing ones. If the benchmark itself is missing, return no rows. Leave all values unrounded.
a.sql:
WITH rating_averages AS (
  SELECT
    rating,
    AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day,
    COUNT(*) AS film_count
  FROM film
  WHERE rental_duration > 5
  GROUP BY rating
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS overall_benchmark
  FROM rating_averages
)
SELECT
  ra.rating,
  ra.avg_rate_per_day,
  ra.film_count,
  ra.avg_rate_per_day / b.overall_benchmark AS relative_to_benchmark
FROM rating_averages ra
CROSS JOIN benchmark b
WHERE b.overall_benchmark IS NOT NULL;

c.request: Treating 5 days as the cutoff for a long rental period, look only at the long-rental films (by `rental_duration`) and group them by `rating`. For each rating, show the rating, the average per film of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values), the number of films, and that average divided by an overall benchmark. The benchmark is the plain unweighted mean of the per-rating averages across all ratings, ignoring any missing ones. If the benchmark itself is missing, return no rows. Leave all values unrounded. Keep only films whose rental duration is strictly more than 5 days, so films with exactly 5 days are left out.
c.sql:
WITH rating_averages AS (
  SELECT
    rating,
    AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day,
    COUNT(*) AS film_count
  FROM film
  WHERE rental_duration > 5
  GROUP BY rating
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS overall_benchmark
  FROM rating_averages
)
SELECT
  ra.rating,
  ra.avg_rate_per_day,
  ra.film_count,
  ra.avg_rate_per_day / b.overall_benchmark AS relative_to_benchmark
FROM rating_averages AS ra
CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b
WHERE b.overall_benchmark IS NOT NULL
